newsitem.title: UK: Reuters appoints two new executive directors.
newsitem.headline: Reuters appoints two new executive directors.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc named two new executive directors on Monday and announced the merger of its Europe, Middle East and Africa management with that of its UK and Ireland division.
Jean-Claude Marchand was named executive director to head the newly-merged European, Middle East and Africa division.

The other new director, John Parcell, formerly head of the UK and Ireland division, has been placed in charge of the company's financial information product line that generates the majority of Reuters revenue, the company said in a statement.
Editor-in-chief Mark Wood intends to step down as an executive director, the international news and information company said.

Wood's move comes as the company shifts to a new arrangement under which he will report directly to the board, as well as to the board of Reuters Trustees, on editorial matters including the independence and quality of the newsfile, Reuters said.
Marchand, 50, is Swiss and joined Reuters as a sales executive in Switzerland in 1971.
He has since served in a wide range of country and regional management positions in Europe and Asia/Pacific, latterly being in charge of Continental Europe, Middle East and Africa.

Reuters said of Parcell, 50, that his 27-year career with the company has spanned country and regional management in Latin America and Europe, as well as positions in marketing and product management.
Wood, 44, will report to chief executive Peter Job and will continue to represent Reuters on the board of Britain's Independent Television News (ITN).

Marchand will deputise for executive director Andre Villeneuve, who is in charge of all geographical areas, while Parcell will deputise for David Ure, who is responsible for global marketing and product development, the statement said.
Finance director Rob Rowley will take on additional responsibility for media and new business ventures outside the financial sector, the statement added.
Reuters Holdings shares were down five pence at 753-1/2 following the announcement, in the context of a sharply lower London share market.
